name: ARPL index
description: Machine-readable index of ARPL instruction packs. Generated by tools/build_catalogs.py; read AGENTS.md for how to use it.
staleness: Two triggers. review_due is one year after the last evidence (recorded date or latest reproduction). unverified_in_current_revit is true when the pack was not tested in the latest Revit release (vocabularies revit_releases). Either one: verify the result as if the pack were new.
provenance: Record every pack you used as {arpl_pack, pack_revision, revit_version, result}. To pin exact content, replace main in raw_base with a commit SHA or release tag.
read_order_per_pack: failure_patterns listed in the manifest, full text in failure_patterns_file

work_classes.W1: Component family authoring (driven by a source and an LOD)
work_classes.W2: Adaptive / form-driven geometry (driven by a rig)
work_classes.W3: Layout-driven assembly production (driven by a rule applied many times)
work_classes.W4: Building model authoring (driven by a program and system families)
work_classes.W5: Model change and propagation (driven by one changed fundamental)
work_classes.W6: Documentation production (driven by views and sheets)
work_classes.W7: Information and data (driven by parameters, standards, quantities)
work_classes.W8: Analysis and review (driven by questions about an existing model)

project_workflows.title: ADU exterior wall fabrication package (LOD 400 + BOM)
project_workflows.intent: Turn the exterior walls of a one-storey wood-frame ADU into prefabricated wall panels: 2x6 framing, 3/4in plywood, bevel siding, XPS cavity fill; one assembly per wall; shop drawings; BOM and cost.

steps.do: Build and flex-test component families (lumber, sheet panel, insulation block, siding board)
Write the layout rule (studs 16in o.c., 3-stud corners, double top plate lapped, openings with king/jack/header/sill/cripples, sheets on stud centres, siding courses, foam per cavity)
2D preview from the rule: studs in plan, sheet and board joints in elevations; user confirms or corrects the rule
Resolve design conflicts found by the preview as user decisions (door lowered to fit a header) and re-preview
Replay the rule in 3D per wall; disallow joins on all framing; verify every piece; group into assemblies
Assembly shop drawings: framing and sheathing elevations, plan section, 3D, part list; trade dimension style; PDF review
Quantities and cost from the model; governed BOM parameters
Issue: one shop drawing sheet per panel that differs (identical panels once, with a quantity), add every assembly sheet to the print set, export the set to PDF, open the PDF and check each sheet
Synchronize with central after the package passes its checks, with a comment; on cloud models save local before and after (operating rule in AGENTS.md)

project_workflows.title: ADU shed roof assembly (LOD 400 + BOM): framing, deck, standing seam, trim, insulation
project_workflows.intent: Replace a placeholder shed roof with a real build-up and turn it into one roof assembly: 2x8 rafters @ 24in, walls rebuilt to fit the roof (taller high wall, raked end walls), frieze blocks, outlookers and fly rafters, 3/4in plywood deck, standing seam roofing, 1x10 fascia and barge boards covering every exposed rafter cut, batts and drywall inside the wall lines, shop drawing and BOM with cost.

steps.do: Read the roof as modelled before planning: type, slope, footprint, overhangs, height gap between flat wall plates and the sloped roof underside, neighbouring elements (e.g. a trellis under the eave)

Ask the decisions that belong to the user: structure (rafters on walls built to fit the roof vs trusses), member size (engineer flag), roofing for the slope (5 deg excludes asphalt shingles), overhangs, trim, soffit, insulation, assembly grouping
2D preview from the layout rule: framing plan, sheathing plan, section; check every view direction; look at the exported images

Replace the placeholder roof: new footprint roof with the real layers (Revit 2024 cannot edit roof sketches or attach walls by API), user re-attaches the walls, then delete the old roof; guard every transaction
Component families: lumber types 2x8 / 2x4 flat; work-plane-based copies of sheet and insulation families; flex-test the plane orientation

Build from one layout rule in a dry run with an all-pairs clash check; offset square-cut ends by depth x sin(slope); commit only with allow-listed contacts; trim must cover every exposed cut; insulation only inside the exterior wall lines
Create the assembly after Regenerate; name it after commit
BOM from the model: check every piece against its stock size; reset Cost and Type Comments on duplicated types; price with source and date; stock conversion, waste, tax, range
Shop drawing: framing plan with deck hidden, deck layout, section along the slope, 3D, parts list, dimensions one per transaction, BOM note; export and look at the sheet

project_workflows.title: Weekly BIM coordination of a federated cloud project: collect, check, correct, report, archive
project_workflows.intent: Keep a federated cloud project current in one weekly session: collect model data in an unattended batch, add LOIN completeness and a clash run, check everything against fixed rules and last week's snapshot, repair what is safe to repair, queue the rest for approval, and publish one dashboard report with recommendations for the team.

steps.do: Preflight: Revit idle at Home with no model open (ask before closing the user's work), bridge alive, disk and collaboration cache space, registry compared with the cloud folder (new or renamed models), report folder REPORTS/<date> created

Collect in batch (unattended): Model Health Check and PBP + Worksets report over all registry models, then Export Schedules (instance parameters, project information, sheet list); output folder typed explicitly

Collect deep, read-only: shared position at the internal origin per model against the authority, link instances per host with workset and total transform (links loaded, not from the batch report), Project Information keys, standard schedules present; Project Status (also in the PROJECT-INFO export) and the model's phase list (Document.Phases, names in order) for the status and phase checks

LOIN snapshot: from the exported instance-parameter schedules count filled values per model, category and field (family elements only); score against the client's LOIN table, or state the assumption. Count by unique id; before reporting a field at 0% as a team task, trace it to its source (circuit values, unenclosed spaces). Data alignment between runs (mirror parameters, instance key, Type Marks, room-bounding links) is coordinator work under docs/roles/bim-coordinator.md

Clash run: open the discipline models in one session (link worksets closed), intersect the agreed category pairs, separate penetrations, group clashes, owner by routing priority; close the models unsaved. Use the cloud clash service instead where the project has one
Check: one dataset per source (models, links, warnings, LOIN, clashes) keyed by model or pair and week; findings per model and rule; week-over-week deltas from the second week on

Correct: safe fixes automatically (repair links to the matrix, missing building name, missing standard schedules, then sync); anything that moves geometry, changes coordinates or deletes waits for the coordinator's approval

Report: one dashboard page in the standard report form ARPL-RPT-0001 (report/STANDARD.md: headline, tiles, recommendations, clashes, LOIN, warnings, checks, link matrix, model contents, not collected) over its five datasets; every number drawn from the datasets, none typed

Print: one PDF booklet per model in the same unattended batch (ACC Gate 'Print PDFs from Print Intel workbooks'); set-up once per model: fixed print set, Print Intel workbook, PrintJobs row; check page counts against the sets and run the drift check when sheets change
Archive: keep raw outputs in REPORTS/<date>; append the week's datasets to history; submit new lessons to the ARPL inbox (Revit and ZEN alike)

packs.title: Assembly naming and identical panels
use_when: creating and naming Revit assemblies
several identical panels or modules need drawings
packs.lesson: Revit detects identical assemblies and gives them one type.

packs.title: Device placement follows the framing (manufacturer's standpoint)
use_when: placing receptacles, switches, lights, smoke alarms, floor boxes or other devices in framed walls, roofs or floors
layout previews for prefab wall, roof or floor panels
not_for: devices on concrete or masonry without framing (use slab sleeve / chase rules)
deciding code compliance (the code checks still apply)
packs.lesson: A layout that satisfies the code but ignores the framing is not buildable as drawn; the fabricator moves the device, and the drawings become wrong.

packs.title: Vertical studs pulled by auto-joins
use_when: placing vertical studs, posts or braces as structural framing
framing members end up longer or shifted after placement
not_for: structural columns (not framing)
packs.lesson: Revit framing joins change members after placement, including their position.

packs.title: Door too tall for a header
use_when: framing a wall with openings where headers must fit under top plates
a door or window rough opening is close to the plate height
not_for: openings in non-framed walls (masonry, concrete)
packs.lesson: Conflicts between the architecture and the framing rule surface in the layout computation; they are design decisions, not things to fix silently.

packs.title: Plywood slivers at openings
use_when: laying out sheathing, sheet goods or cladding boards across a wall with openings
deciding where panel joints fall relative to windows and doors
not_for: curtain walls
single full-height sheets without openings
packs.lesson: Material constraints must be part of the layout rule, not a check afterwards; and a fix needs the same preview as the original rule.

packs.title: Slab on grade from the framing layout (anchors, recess, stub-ups)
use_when: a prefab timber building sits on a slab on grade
anchor bolts, slab recesses or plumbing stub-ups must match wall panels and fixtures
not_for: structural design of the slab or anchorage (engineer of record)
raised floors on piers or ground screws
packs.lesson: The slab is the first prefab assembly on site: everything that lands on it (plates, posts, drains, water service) is already known from the panels and fixtures, so the slab layout is derived, not drawn.

packs.title: Sloped roof assembly from component families
use_when: framing and finishing a sloped (shed, mono-pitch) roof as an assembly of lumber, sheet and board families
placing sheet goods, insulation or trim on a sloped plane
covering rafter tails and fly rafters with fascia and barge boards
not_for: prefabricated trusses modelled as single families
curved roofs
packs.lesson: Sloped assemblies need work-plane-based component families and an explicit orientation rule; on a slope every square-cut end moves by depth x sin(slope), which is where nearly all clashes came from.

test_runs.note: after parameterization: kind falls back to Category: Family Type

inputs.ASSEMBLY_PREFIXES: assembly type name prefixes, empty = all assemblies
inputs.ALLOW: intended contacts, 'Kind A x Kind B'

model_assumptions: The pieces to check are members of assemblies
Piece kind comes from Comments when filled (ARPL build scripts), otherwise from Category: Family Type
Solid geometry exists for every piece (DirectShapes and family instances); linked models are not checked
not_for: Clash checks between linked models (use Navisworks or a link-aware check)
Proving structural adequacy: a clash-free model can still be wrong

packs.title: Revit Parts for wall layers: a dead end
use_when: splitting wall layers into separate fabrication pieces
considering Revit Parts (PartUtils.CreateParts) for panels or BOM
not_for: Parts for simple area takeoffs or visual layer display
packs.lesson: The 'native' Revit route isn't always the production route; established tools are precedents.

packs.title: Power connector without load parameters
use_when: adding electrical power connectors to equipment families
connecting a family to an electrical circuit
not_for: piping or duct connectors
packs.lesson: The PowerCircuit connector type carries no load data.

packs.title: Residential branch circuits from a confirmed layout
use_when: electrical for a small dwelling unit or ADU: panel, receptacles, lighting, smoke alarms, circuits
placing wall and ceiling devices by API on host-wall faces and ceiling planes
creating circuits and a panel schedule by API
not_for: commercial distribution or three-phase systems
load calculations or code compliance sign-off (electrical engineer / AHJ)
conduit or cable routing
packs.lesson: A residential electrical layout is a rule check first and a modelling task second; most failures came from content (template families built for commercial work) and from Revit dialogs outside the script's reach.

packs.title: Weekly clash run inside Revit by solid intersection across open cloud models; penetrations separated, clashes grouped, owner by routing priority
use_when: A federated project needs a weekly clash number per discipline pair and the cloud project has no clash service (no Model Coordination module)
Clash results must carry element unique ids so next week's run can report new and resolved clashes
A quick hard-clash check before publishing models for formal coordination
not_for: Clearance (soft) clashes: needs inflated solids, not recorded yet
Walls and floors against services when the service openings are not modelled: every crossing would count
Models that do not share one internal origin and shared position: transform one side by the link transform first
Replacing a coordination service where one is available: use its tracked clash groups instead
packs.lesson: A clash number is only useful per discipline pair, grouped, with owners and stable element ids; a raw intersection count mixes planned penetrations with real conflicts and jumps whenever one run is rerouted.

packs.title: MEP spaces that exist but have no area: set the architectural (and facade) link types to Room Bounding in the MEP model
use_when: Space: Number / Space: Name are empty in MEP schedules although spaces are placed
Spaces report area 0 or 'Not enclosed' in a model that links the architecture
not_for: Moving, deleting or renumbering spaces: that needs the discipline lead
Overlapping space volumes (upper limit / offset): report them to the lead
packs.lesson: A placed space with no area is usually a link that is not room bounding; fix the link type, not the spaces.

packs.title: Shop drawings: invalid references and swapped elevations
use_when: creating dimensioned shop drawings or assembly sheets
adding many dimensions by script
packs.lesson: Per-element transactions contain failures; implicit state (assembly transforms) can't be trusted.

packs.title: Project units round framing dimensions
use_when: dimensioning fabrication or shop drawings for a trade
dimensions round to project units and hide small values
packs.lesson: Project units are set for the architecture, not for fabrication drawings.

packs.title: Weekly print-set booklets with ZEN: one Revit print set per model, Print Intel workbook, ACC Gate Print PDFs
use_when: A federated project needs one PDF booklet per model every week without opening the models by hand
The ZEN add-in (Tiverit LLC) is installed and the project has a ZEN model registry of ACC cloud models
An agent prepares print sets in Revit and drives ZEN Print Intel and ACC Gate from a bridge with screen access
not_for: Projects without ZEN: export PDFs per model from the bridge with PDFExportOptions instead (same content rule, same read-back)
Sets that must follow the sheet list automatically: a Revit print set is a fixed list (see rule 9)
packs.lesson: The weekly booklet is three layers: a fixed Revit print set per model (made once, checked weekly for drift), a ZEN Print Intel workbook that names it in PrintJobs, and one ACC Gate run over the registry. Decide the content by script, build the set in Revit's own dialog, read it back before syncing, and count PDF pages against the workbook.

validation_checks.returns: {check, model, pass, set_existed, count, expected, would_add, would_remove, non_sheet_views, schedule_only, skipped}

inputs.SET: print set name, the same in every model
inputs.SCHEDULES_COUNT: true when schedule-only and panel-schedule sheets belong in the set (the user decides)

test_runs.model: Snowdon Towers sample, 6 models (55, 12, 27, 26, 17 and 2 sheets)
test_runs.note: run before creation (set_existed false, lists the content) and after creation (would_add 0, would_remove 0, non_sheet_views 0) in every model

model_assumptions: Placeholder sheets are never in the set
Title-block revision schedules do not count as content
not_for: Proving that linked content appears on the sheets: check the PDF

packs.title: Annotation family from a newer Revit version
use_when: loading or editing annotation families (tags, labels)
loading a family saved in another Revit version
packs.lesson: File version, file name and reload behaviour all decide whether a family update succeeds.

packs.title: Coffee brewer from a spec sheet: overall height short
use_when: building an equipment family from a manufacturer spec sheet or drawing
overall dimensions don't match after modelling
packs.lesson: Overall dimensions on a spec sheet can include parts that the main views don't label separately.

packs.title: Template with hidden geometry
use_when: choosing a family template for a new family
family geometry is invisible or too large after building
packs.lesson: Some family templates carry hidden default geometry.

packs.title: Faucet on the wrong side: mirrored source view
use_when: modelling from orthographic views of a source drawing
deciding left/right or front/back orientation of a product
packs.lesson: Drawing views in manufacturer sheets can be mirrored.

packs.title: Component families for a wall panel
use_when: building parametric component families for lumber, sheets, insulation or cladding
families that must flex reliably before mass placement
packs.lesson: Parametric component families can be generated reliably when every face is locked to a labelled reference plane.

packs.title: Forms absorb model lines and break hosting
use_when: building adaptive components or forms from profiles
hosted elements lose their host after form edits
not_for: non-adaptive loadable families
packs.lesson: Forms take ownership of model lines used as profiles.

packs.title: Concept model from a neutral spec: staged, idempotent build with visual gates
use_when: An agent builds a whole concept model from a structured spec (JSON) through a code-execution bridge
A build script creates many elements of several categories in one call
Element heights depend on a host (roof, slab) that may change later
The model must show which geometry is source fact and which is an AI estimate
Receiving a neutral spec from USG: rule 8 (evidence tags 'USG | exact / derived / approximate') is the USG-to-ARPL handoff
not_for: Detailed design or construction documentation (LOD 300+)
Workshared central models (no sync handling covered here)
Interpreting the sketch itself: that belongs to USG (see IN-0011 redirect)
packs.lesson: 'Committed' is not 'correct' and 'timed out' is not 'failed'. A spec-driven build needs small idempotent stages, semantic type checks, version-checked API calls, host-derived dependent heights and a visual gate after every stage.

packs.title: Gable walls without wall attachment
use_when: walls under gable or sloped roofs
walls that should follow a roof slope
packs.lesson: Profile walls replace attachment in the 2024 API, but they no longer follow levels (see W5-001).

packs.title: Masterplan from a neutral rebuild package: floors, DirectShape envelopes and domain-based grids
use_when: A neutral package of levels, floor profiles and exact envelopes must become native Revit elements
Exact source mass geometry (triangle face loops) has to enter Revit as DirectShape
Grids must be created for many buildings at once, including rotated wings and curved (arc) buildings
A payload is too large to embed in a code-execution call
not_for: Reading or interpreting the original source model (upstream intake, USG)
Structural design: grid intersections are column-centreline candidates only
Workshared central models
packs.lesson: A neutral rebuild package becomes native Revit quickly and exactly when data travels as files, every element is identified by name or Mark (not by a parameter that may not exist), envelopes are pre-checked for closure, and visual checks use API image export rather than the desktop UI.

packs.title: Footing corner notches
use_when: modelling foundations or footings at wall corners
relying on automatic joins at corners
packs.lesson: Wall joins assumed by the UI don't happen through the API.

packs.title: Batch-link cloud models from a registry and link matrix, placed by shared coordinates; verify by link transform
use_when: Every model of a federated cloud project must link the others, driven by a registry and a host-by-link matrix
A batch tool generated the link matrix and its settings must be checked before the run
Link placement has to be proven after the run
not_for: Projects whose models do not share one coordinate system: set coordinates first (ARPL-LNK-0001)
Local file links
packs.lesson: A generated link configuration must be read before a batch run: defaults can contradict the project's coordinate setup. After the run, placement is proven by the link transform, not by looking.

packs.title: Set shared coordinates on an authority building, then split a campus model into per-building files
use_when: A campus or masterplan model has to be split into per-building models that will be linked back by shared coordinates
One building is the coordinate authority and the site location comes from a map pick (lat/long) rather than a survey file
Elements (grids, masses, floors) must be assigned to buildings automatically before a split
not_for: Projects with a surveyed control point or a civil/site model to acquire coordinates from: acquire from that instead
Splits where buildings share elements that cannot be assigned to one building (shared podium, site-wide topography): decide ownership first
packs.lesson: Set shared coordinates once in the parent before splitting, so every child inherits them; assign elements to buildings by containment, never by nearest distance.

packs.title: Batch-onboard local models to the cloud and register each one: verify by document state, handle posted-command dialogs
use_when: An agent uploads or registers a series of local models to one cloud project folder
A bridge call outlasts the bridge's reply wait (cloud save, enable worksharing, sync)
An add-in command started by PostCommand opens file pickers, confirmation prompts or result dialogs
Some models may already exist in the cloud folder, uploaded earlier by someone else
not_for: Single interactive uploads done by a person
Batch tools that already run headless without dialogs: use those and skip the screen handling
packs.lesson: In a batch of cloud uploads, the bridge reply is not the result: long calls time out, failures can arrive late and leave a misleading PathName, and posted commands open dialogs that block the bridge. Verify each step by document state, keep each call short, and drive dialogs by keyboard with a focus guard.

packs.title: An exception inside an open Transaction crashed Revit
use_when: any scripted change that starts its own Transaction, especially inside a TransactionGroup
a bridge or add-in runs agent-written C# against a live model
not_for: read-only scripts that open no transaction
packs.lesson: In Revit 2024 an exception that leaves a scripted Transaction open while an enclosing TransactionGroup is aborted can crash Revit, not just fail the script. The first visible error (ArgumentNullException) was harmless; the crash came from the unclosed transaction.

packs.title: Reset a workshared cloud model: remove all Revit links and delete user worksets with all worksets closed
use_when: batch-clean several workshared cloud (ACC/BIM 360) models before a relinking run, a demo or a standards reset
delete user worksets and move their elements to Workset1 without opening the worksets
remove every RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance from a host model
not_for: detaching or archiving models (use DetachFromCentral instead)
non-workshared files
removing CAD imports or links (ImportInstance, CADLinkType)

packs.title: ZEN ACC Gate as the weekly collection batch: health, links and worksets, schedule exports; what each output contains and how to drive it from a bridge
use_when: The ZEN add-in (Tiverit LLC) is installed and a project has a ZEN model registry
A weekly coordination run needs per-model health, link placement and schedule data without opening each model by hand
An agent drives ZEN commands from a Revit bridge
not_for: Projects without ZEN: collect the same data with read-only bridge scripts (ARPL-PW-0003 lists the fields)
Cloud file sizes: they need ZEN's Refresh Sizes with APS credentials
packs.lesson: ZEN's ACC Gate collects most of the weekly data in one unattended batch, but its reports describe the models as the batch opened them (links unloaded), and every dialog default must be read, not trusted.

packs.title: Lowering a level: what doesn't follow
use_when: changing a level elevation or another fundamental datum
a change must propagate to walls, roofs, openings and layouts
packs.lesson: Constraint-driven elements follow a level; sketch-driven ones don't.

packs.title: Changing a footprint roof's outline by API in Revit 2024
use_when: changing the outline, overhangs or type of an existing footprint roof by script
replacing a placeholder roof with a real roof type while walls are attached to it
not_for: extrusion roofs
roofs edited by hand in sketch mode
Revit versions where wall attachment and roof sketch editing are available in the API (check before applying)
packs.lesson: Revit 2024's API cannot edit a footprint roof's sketch or attach walls to a roof. Changing the outline means a new roof, and the wall attachment is a user step.

packs.title: Markup read without checking the camera
use_when: interpreting markups or redlines on a 3D view or screenshot
reviewing feedback given on a 3D image
packs.lesson: A screenshot carries no orientation unless you read it from the view.

packs.title: LOIN instance schedule per discipline: mirror category values into project parameters and give every instance a contractor key (discipline, element code, room or level, number)
use_when: A client or project requires an information delivery per discipline (LOIN, ISO 19650 / ISO 7817-1) and a weekly dataset is read from one standard instance schedule per model
Contractors, bidders or site staff need to name one instance unambiguously (this door, not the door type)
The multi-category schedule cannot show a category-specific value (voltage, flow, fire rating, element id)
not_for: Type identification: Type Mark stays the type key (see ARPL-PAR-0004)
Asset tagging for operations, where the client gives its own asset code scheme
packs.lesson: The schedule shows only what the instance itself holds: mirror the values the data needs into project parameters, key every instance once, and count the export by unique id.

packs.title: Governed material Descriptions and Keynotes
use_when: A Revit material schedule contains blank, incomplete or contradictory Description values.
Materials need Keynote values for material tags or sheet keynote legends.
Material data is exported to CSV, AI-reviewed and read back into Revit.
A Revit Bridge reads material properties, requests an AI proposal, previews the proposal and commits approved changes.
not_for: Inventing manufacturer, product, grade, performance or specification properties that are not supported by the source data.
Replacing an approved office or project keynote database without explicit authorization.
Treating appearance assets as authoritative physical specifications.
Automatically describing analytical, phase, poche, default or other graphic/system materials as construction materials unless the user explicitly wants them documented.
Merging, deduplicating, renaming or deleting Revit materials as a side effect of metadata enrichment.
packs.lesson: Separate the four identities of a Revit material: Name is the BIM identifier, Description is the human-readable material identity, Keynote is the documentation/tagging identity, and Appearance is the visual identity. AI reasoning may be rich and probabilistic; production BIM data must remain authorized, deterministic and verifiable.

packs.title: One shared parameter file per company: find every candidate, choose one master, edit it byte-exact, keep project parameters in a project group
use_when: Starting coordinator work on a project and the shared parameter file in use is not known
Two teams report the same parameter with different GUIDs, or schedules lose values after a family reload
A typo in a shared parameter name must be fixed without breaking existing values
not_for: Annotation families that carry the review stamp (QAQC note block): those are families loaded into the model, not entries in the shared parameter file
Deciding the company's parameter naming standard: that is the owner's decision
packs.lesson: A shared parameter is its GUID, not its name: keep one file, rename in place with the GUID unchanged, and write the file exactly as Revit wrote it.

packs.title: Type Marks with ZEN Type Marks by Family: one run per family group, the search string becomes the prefix, Overwrite on for a clean re-run
use_when: A model has no or inconsistent Type Marks and the types can be grouped by a word in the family name
Type Marks must be redone after the grouping changed
not_for: Pipe, duct and fitting system types (no family-name group); leave them or mark them by system
Firm-specific code lists that do not follow family names: enter the code as the search string only if family names contain it
packs.lesson: In ZEN Type Marks by Family the search string is the prefix: run once per group, Overwrite on, and check that family names really contain the string.

packs.title: Door swing reported correct without a test
use_when: placing, swapping or flipping doors
reporting door swing or hand
packs.lesson: FacingOrientation doesn't reliably predict the swing.

packs.title: Windows placed at sill 0
use_when: placing windows, doors or other hosted families by script
packs.lesson: API placement doesn't apply UI defaults.

packs.title: BOM from governed instance data: deduplicated QTO grouped by a category rule table, every line traced to its model elements (implements ARPL-BOM-0001)
use_when: A GC or estimator needs quantities to buy against from a federation that exports a standard instance-parameter schedule with instance keys
A quantity must be traced back to the model elements that make it up
not_for: Procurement quantities (waste, purchase units, suppliers): those need the GC item table
Projects without instance keys or unique ids in the export: run ARPL-PAR-0003 first
packs.lesson: A BOM is a deterministic grouping of deduplicated instance data under a governed rule table. Every input row ends in a BOM line or a named exception. Parts follow the unit the trade buys. The export must carry the quantity the trade buys by. Wrong categories surface as BOM lines.

packs.title: Cost per type can't carry a BOM
use_when: preparing a bill of materials (BOM) or cut list from families
adding cost or quantity fields to schedules
packs.lesson: A BOM needs governed fields decided before the families are built.

packs.title: Cost estimate priced the wrong construction
use_when: estimating material or construction costs from a model
pricing wall, floor or roof types
packs.lesson: Type names describe a material, not a construction method.

packs.title: Layout preview as a review step
use_when: any layout-driven build: studs, panels, cladding, tiles, ceiling grids
before committing many repeated elements in 3D
not_for: single elements
packs.lesson: A preview is a review tool, not decoration.

packs.title: LOIN completeness snapshot from an exported instance-parameter schedule: fill rate per model, field and category, family elements only
use_when: The client asks where the project stands on information requirements (LOIN) and every model carries the same instance-parameter schedule
A weekly report needs a completeness number and a ranked list of gaps
not_for: Checking values for correctness: this counts filled, not right
Type parameters that the schedule does not show per instance
packs.lesson: LOIN completeness is only meaningful against the client's requirement per category; until that table exists, state the assumption next to the number.

packs.title: Crops silently ignored
use_when: setting crop boxes or scope boxes on views
exported views show more than intended
packs.lesson: Some settings override others without any error.

packs.title: Section looking the wrong way
use_when: creating sections or elevations by script
a new section or elevation looks the wrong way
packs.lesson: View direction conventions must be checked, not assumed.

failure_patterns.name: Geometry correct, semantics wrong
Wrong coordinate frame or orientation
Existing content should have been reused
Missing fabrication or material constraint
